draft.title: Folding and faulting
card: Rock in the Earth's crust is made of layers. Huge forces push, pull and slide the crust, and the rock changes shape.
layers of rock bend into waves when they are squeezed. The layers stay joined and do not break.
rock cracks when the force is too strong for it to bend. The crack is called a fault.
Blocks of rock on either side of a fault can move up, down or sideways. The movement can build landforms such as ridges and steep slopes.
draft.remember: Folding bends rock into waves. Faulting cracks it and moves the blocks.

a.q: Layers of rock are squeezed and bend into waves without breaking. What is this called?
opts: Folding
Faulting
Weathering
Erosion
a.why: Layers that bend into waves while staying joined are folded. Faulting is the tempting wrong answer, because it involves rock cracking and blocks moving, and these layers did not break.
a.clue: Did the rock break or did it bend?

b.q: A road cutting in Tasmania shows rock layers with a long crack. The layers on one side of the crack sit much higher than the same layers on the other side. What most likely happened?
opts: Faulting moved one block of rock up past the other
Folding bent the layers into a wave without cracking
Folding pushed the layers up and left a crack behind
Faulting bent the layers into a wave, still joined
b.why: A crack with matching layers at different heights shows that blocks moved along a fault. Folding is tempting because layers have moved, but folded layers bend and stay joined without a crack.
b.clue: Look for a crack with the layers out of line.

b.best: Faulting moved one block of rock up past the other

problems.detail: "Rock in the Earth's crust is made of layers" overgeneralises. Much crustal rock, such as granite and other igneous rock, is not layered. Better: "Much of the rock in the Earth's crust is in layers."

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer (Folding; Faulting moved one block up past the other). One minor fact issue: the card says all crustal rock is layered, when only some of it is.

a.q: Rock layers in a cliff curve up and down like waves, with no cracks through them. What most likely formed this shape?

Cracking of the rock along a fault
Blocks of rock sliding past each other
Pulling that split the layers apart
